tasks.title: Lecture #58
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an anthropology class.
tasks.transcript: Man: In the first half of the 20th century, an anthropological movement emerged,called the Culture and Personality School. According to the Culture and Personality school, people's personalities are a result of the culture they live in, and not just based on biology, like not just inherited from their biological parents. For example, how children in a culture experience food, the foods they eat, how it's prepared, this shapes their individual tastes and preferences. One of the anthropologists most associated with this movement was Ruth Benedict. Benedict studied and embraced the principles of cultural relativism. So according to cultural relativism, all cultures should be studied on their own terms and not judged against some external measure. So cultures in, say, Egypt, belong to Egypt and shouldn't be the standard of what all cultures should try to be. Ruth Benedict refuted the dominant anthropology theory at the time, which stated that there was a hierarchy of cultures, some advanced, others not. Rejecting that took courage. And I think the field is better for it. Benedict was also influenced by psychology, especially Gestalt ideas. According to Gestalt psychology, a personality is an integrated whole, not just a list of traits. Like, If you see a painting of a landscape, you're looking at a whole landscape and not just say, a hill, trees and a farmhouse. Benedict said that cultures were the same way, a whole coherent system with patterns of values and behaviors, and more than just a set of characteristics.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker refer to children's experiences with food?

options.A: To provide an example of how culture can influence personality
options.B: To explain how people's tastes and preferences can be based on biology
options.C: To contrast Ruth Benedict's ideas with another perspective
options.D: To identify a problem with a claim made by the Culture and Personality School

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目的意思是：演讲者为什么提到儿童对食物的体验？ 选项分析： A. To provide an example of how culture can influence personality. 演讲者在介绍“文化与人格学派”的核心观点（文化塑造人格）后，紧接着用了"For example"引出儿童饮食体验的例子，说明文化环境如何塑造个人的口味和偏好，以此支撑核心观点，符合题意。原文定位句： “For example, how children in a culture experience food… this shapes their individual tastes and preferences.” B. To explain how people’s tastes and preferences can be based on biology. 观点恰恰相反，演讲者强调的是“not just based on biology”（不仅仅基于生物学）。 C. To contrast Ruth Benedict’s ideas with another perspective. 这个例子是用来解释学派的基本观点，并未用来做对比。 D. To identify a problem with a claim made by the Culture and Personality School. 演讲者是在阐述该学派的观点，并未指出问题。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention Egypt?

options.A: To indicate where Ruth Benedict began comparing cultures
options.B: To introduce a theory by an Egyptian anthropologist
options.C: To illustrate an idea that guided Ruth Benedict's work
options.D: To point out a culture that should be a standard for others

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目的意思是：演讲者为什么提到埃及？ 选项分析： A. To indicate where Ruth Benedict began comparing cultures. 文中未提及本尼迪克特的研究起点是埃及。 B. To introduce a theory by an Egyptian anthropologist. 文中未提及埃及人类学家。 C. To illustrate an idea that guided Ruth Benedict’s work. 演讲者提到埃及是为了举例说明“文化相对主义”这一指导本尼迪克特工作的原则：每种文化都应按其自身标准被研究，而不应成为其他文化的标准。原文定位句： “So according to cultural relativism… So cultures in, say, Egypt, belong to Egypt and shouldn’t be the standard of what all cultures should try to be.” D. To point out a culture that should be a standard for others. 观点相反，演讲者说埃及文化“shouldn’t be the standard”（不应成为标准）。

questions.stem: What impresses the speaker about Ruth Benedict?

options.A: Benedict's determination to apply psychology theories to anthropology
options.B: Benedict's fairness in creating a hierarchy of cultures
options.C: Benedict's ability to teach people about different cultures
options.D: Benedict's willingness to contradict an established idea

questions.analysis: 答案：D 题目的意思是：关于鲁思·本尼迪克特，什么让演讲者印象深刻？ 选项分析： A. Benedict’s determination to apply psychology theories to anthropology. 虽然提到了心理学影响，但这并不是演讲者强调的“令人印象深刻”的点。 B. Benedict’s fairness in creating a hierarchy of cultures. 本尼迪克特是反驳了等级制度，而不是创立等级制度。 C. Benedict’s ability to teach people about different cultures. 文中强调的是她的理论贡献和勇气，而非教学能力。 D. Benedict’s willingness to contradict an established idea. 演讲者提到本尼迪克特反驳了当时占主导地位的“文化等级论”，并评价说“Rejecting that took courage”（拒绝那个观点需要勇气），这种勇气即愿意挑战既定观念，符合题意。原文定位句： “Ruth Benedict refuted the dominant anthropology theory at the time… Rejecting that took courage.”

questions.stem: What does the speaker suggest about a painting of a landscape?

options.A: It reflects the values of the painter's culture.
options.B: It is more than the individual elements pictured in it.
options.C: Its meaning depends on the viewer's cultural expectations.
options.D: Its patterns are meaningful for Gestalt psychologists.

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目的意思是：演讲者关于风景画暗示了什么？ 选项分析： A. It reflects the values of the painter’s culture. 这里是用画作比喻文化的整体性，并未涉及画家的文化价值观。 B. It is more than the individual elements pictured in it. 演讲者用风景画做类比，指出看画是看“a whole landscape”（整体风景），而不仅仅是山丘、树木或农舍的堆砌。这暗示了整体大于部分之和，符合题意。原文定位句： “Like, If you see a painting of a landscape, you’re looking at a whole landscape and not just say, a hill, trees and a farmhouse.” C. Its meaning depends on the viewer’s cultural expectations. 文中未提及观看者的期待。 D. Its patterns are meaningful for Gestalt psychologists. 演讲者提到格式塔心理学是为了解释本尼迪克特的理论视角，并非在讨论画作对心理学家的意义。
